1. Select and configure Llama

The checkpoint supplies a model configuration; MAX uses that configuration to build a decoder graph. The llama3 name identifies MAX's implementation package. Its registration maps the LlamaForCausalLM architecture name to Llama3Model.

QnA 1Package name · Hugging Face checkpoint · Architecture registrationSOURCE3 questions

1. Where does the package name llama3 come from?

It is the name of an implementation package in MAX's source tree: max.pipelines.architectures.llama3. The built-in registration explicitly connects the checkpoint architecture name to that package.

SOURCE — the exact entry in register_all_models():

_LazyArch("LlamaForCausalLM", ".llama3", "llama_arch"),
Entry Meaning
"LlamaForCausalLM" Architecture name used for lookup
".llama3" Package to import, relative to max.pipelines.architectures
"llama_arch" Registration object to retrieve from the imported package

llama_arch selects the Llama3Model class and the Llama3Config class. The package keeps its name while Llama3Config reads the checkpoint dimensions: hidden size, attention and KV heads, layer count, intermediate size, and vocabulary size. This is why the Llama 2 7B walkthrough enters a directory named llama3. The architecture match selects a candidate implementation; compatible weights, encoding, and settings are still required.

2. What comes from Hugging Face, and how does MAX match it to registered objects?

Hugging Face supplies checkpoint files. MAX supplies the implementation classes and their registration. Files are fetched as needed; the small configuration can be inspected before downloading the large weight files.

Checkpoint asset What it contains Use in the built-in MAX path
config.json Architecture name, dimensions, attention/RoPE settings, and other model metadata Select and configure an implementation
Weight files, commonly .safetensors Learned tensors for embeddings, attention, MLPs, and normalization Supply model parameters
Weight index, when present Tensor-name-to-shard mapping Describe which file contains each tensor; MAX's selected weight loader determines how files are opened
Tokenizer files, such as tokenizer.json or tokenizer.model, plus tokenizer settings Vocabulary, tokenization rules, and special tokens Convert text to token IDs and back
Optional generation_config.json Generation defaults Supply defaults when available; the config loader has a fallback

BOUNDARY — a typical Hugging Face Hub cache layout is shown below. This is an illustration, not an inspection of a downloaded Llama checkpoint. The cache root is configurable; snapshots are keyed by checkpoint revision.

~/.cache/huggingface/hub/
└── models--meta-llama--Llama-2-7b-hf/
    ├── refs/
    ├── blobs/
    └── snapshots/<checkpoint-commit>/
        ├── config.json
        ├── <selected weight files>
        └── <tokenizer and other fetched assets>
Entry What it means
~/.cache/huggingface/hub/ Default Hub cache root; HF_HOME or HF_HUB_CACHE can change it.
models--meta-llama--Llama-2-7b-hf/ Cache namespace for the meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf repository.
refs/ Cached branch or tag names, such as main, mapped to the commit each ref resolved to.
blobs/ The downloaded file contents; different revision snapshots can reuse the same blob.
snapshots/<checkpoint-commit>/ The file view for one exact repository commit; entries normally point to the shared blobs.
config.json Model metadata, including model_type, architectures, and dimension settings.
<selected weight files> Learned tensors in the chosen format; large checkpoints can split them into shards.
<tokenizer and other fetched assets> Tokenizer data/settings and optional files such as generation_config.json.

These are cache roles: a snapshot does not mean MAX copied or downloaded every repository file. MAX/Hugging Face resolve the requested revision and fetch the configuration, selected weights, tokenizer files, or generation settings as their loaders need them.

SOURCE — download_weight_files() checks direct local paths, then the Hugging Face cache, then downloads as needed. Configuration uses AutoConfig.from_pretrained(), tokenization uses AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(), and generation defaults use GenerationConfig.from_pretrained().

The AutoConfig call raises a broader question: how does max serve move from checkpoint metadata and registry selection through tokenizer and weight loading to MAX's finalized Llama3Config? Expand nested QnA 1.1; its QnA 1.1.x cells trace each path.

QnA 1.1 · Checkpoint-to-model call pathsConfig · registration · tokenizer · generation defaults · weights · Llama3ConfigCall stack tree ↗

AutoConfig here is Hugging Face Transformers; it is not MAX's Llama3Config. For a normal Llama 2 7B Transformers checkpoint, config.json contains model_type: "llama". Hugging Face's AutoConfig.from_pretrained() reads that file and selects the Transformers config class, normally transformers.LlamaConfig. MAX then uses the returned metadata to build its own architecture-specific config.

Llama3Config.initialize() combines Hugging Face fields with MAX serving settings. Llama3Config.finalize() uses loaded weight metadata to resolve weight-dependent choices. They are separate from the Transformers config object:

Call or class Defined by Role in Llama 2 7B serving
AutoConfig.from_pretrained(...) Hugging Face Transformers, called by MAX Read config.json and return a Transformers LlamaConfig with dimensions and RoPE settings. The link opens MAX's exact call site.
Llama3Config.initialize(...) MAX Combine checkpoint metadata with devices, dtype, sequence length, quantization encoding, and KV-cache settings.
Llama3Config.finalize(...) MAX Inspect the loaded weight state and finish settings such as quantization, normalization, tied embeddings, and projection layout.

The checkpoint's model_type selects a Transformers config class; its architectures[0] (normally "LlamaForCausalLM") selects a MAX architecture registration. llama3 is MAX's implementation package name, not a package name supplied by this Llama 2 checkpoint.

QnA 1.1.1 · HF config loadingWho calls load_huggingface_config and AutoConfig?

Example commands — specify the task, or let MAX infer it:

max serve --model meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf --task text_generation
max serve --model meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf

Assume the effective configuration does not set task in a config file. The default --headless and --cascade settings choose the standard API-server path shown below.

Call-flow tree — CLI arguments to Hugging Face AutoConfig:

  • @main.command(name="serve", cls=WithLazyPipelineOptions) registers max serve as a Click command whose callback is cli_serve().
  • WithLazyPipelineOptions._ensure_options_loaded() adds the model and pipeline options just before Click parses the command.
    • pipeline_config_options() generates those options from MAX's configuration fields.
    • get_normalized_flag_names() maps the PipelineArgs.model_path field to the user-facing --model flag (and also accepts --model-path). Thus the example value becomes config_kwargs["model_path"] in cli_serve().
  • cli_serve(..., **config_kwargs) is the handler Click invokes after parsing the command. It builds server Settings from server flags such as --host and --port, then turns the model-related keyword arguments into pipeline arguments.
  • PipelineArgs.from_flat_kwargs(**config_kwargs) constructs the immutable PipelineArgs input. CLI options such as --model, --task, and --max-length arrive as keyword fields; when --config-file is used, its YAML values are merged with the CLI values, with explicit CLI values winning for a field. For these commands, it also calls ModelManifest.from_model_path(). The single-model probe builds a temporary model config and can load HF config and generation defaults before task inference, in both examples.
  • PipelineArgs.task defaults to PipelineTask.UNDEFINED. It stays undefined when neither the CLI nor the merged config file specifies a task. That effective value is the condition for task inference; merely omitting --task is not enough if the config file supplies one.
  • serve_api_server_and_model_worker(settings, pipeline_args) is called for the standard server path. --headless uses a worker-only route, and --cascade selects a separate server path.
  • Task inference branch — runs only when pipeline_args.task is PipelineTask.UNDEFINED:
    • PipelineArgs.main_architecture_name asks the model config for the checkpoint's first architectures entry; for the usual Llama 2 7B Hugging Face config this is LlamaForCausalLM.
    • MAXModelConfig.from_pipeline_args() constructs the model metadata needed to inspect the checkpoint.
      • _build_model_config() prepares the repository handle and Hugging Face config.
      • MAXModelConfig._populate_hf_config() loads a config when the repository has a loadable config file.
        • load_huggingface_config() checks MAX's process-wide config cache before asking Transformers to load the config.
        • AutoConfig.from_pretrained(...) is the Transformers call site. It reads checkpoint metadata such as model_type and architectures; it returns a Transformers config object, not MAX's Llama3Config.
    • PipelineRegistry.retrieve_pipeline_task(architecture_name) maps that architecture name to its registered MAX task. The Llama causal-LM registration resolves to text generation, and the handler continues with a copy of PipelineArgs containing that task.
  • Explicit-task branch: if --task text_generation (or a task in the config file) already populated PipelineArgs.task, the UNDEFINED test is false and the architecture-based task-inference prepass is skipped. The checkpoint config is still needed by the full pipeline-config step.
  • PipelineConfig.from_args(pipeline_args) builds the resolved, validated config used by architecture selection and serving. Its model config also needs the Hugging Face config. On the inference branch, and also with an explicit task, the HF loader can reuse the earlier argument-probe result from its process cache. Configuration construction itself performs architecture lookup before retrieve_factory().

The inference branch only discovers the task from checkpoint metadata. It does not construct the Llama model or load the checkpoint's large weight files; those steps are traced in QnA 1.1.5.

QnA 1.1.2 · Architecture registrationWhen does MAX register and import the Llama implementation?

Call-flow tree — when the Llama mapping is recorded, imported, and used:

  • Click option loading calls WithLazyPipelineOptions._add_options(), whose CLI-config import can reach max.pipelines before cli_serve(). On the first package import, max.pipelines.__init__ calls register_all_models().
  • The architecture table includes LlamaForCausalLM → .llama3 / llama_arch. These three values mean: use LlamaForCausalLM as the lookup key; when needed, import .llama3 relative to the architecture package; then read its llama_arch declaration.
  • PipelineRegistry.register_lazy() delegates that mapping to ArchLookup.register_lazy(). This appends the module, symbol, and package tuple to the in-memory _lazy_architectures["LlamaForCausalLM"] table. It records how to import the implementation; it does not import the Llama module, instantiate a Llama3Model, or load model weights. Deferring imports lets MAX register many supported architectures without importing every implementation at startup.
  • First lookup of LlamaForCausalLM materializes that record:
  • With no task specified, PipelineRegistry.retrieve_pipeline_task() needs the architecture's registered task. It calls PipelineRegistry._materialize_lazy() before reading the task table.
  • With a task already specified, PipelineConfig.from_args() calls find_architecture(), then ArchLookup.find() and resolve(). This can materialize the pending entry before retrieve_factory(). Later, retrieve_factory() selects through PipelineRegistry.architecture_for_config(), PipelineRegistry.retrieve_architecture(), ArchLookup.find(), and ArchLookup.resolve(). The pending lazy record is materialized if that lookup needs it.
  • ArchLookup.materialize(name) removes the pending record, calls importlib.import_module() for .llama3, and retrieves the llama_arch symbol from that module.
    • ArchLookup.register(llama_arch) puts the resulting SupportedArchitecture declaration into the in-memory name and (name, task) lookup tables. Future lookups can reuse that registered object instead of importing it again.
    • llama_arch describes the implementation classes and metadata MAX needs, including Llama3Model, Llama3Config, and TextTokenizer. It is an architecture description, not a model instance or a database of checkpoint tensors.
  • The selected declaration is turned into a serving factory:
  • PipelineRegistry.retrieve_factory() uses the architecture declaration to select the tokenizer, model pipeline class, weight adapter, and memory plan. It creates a deferred factory; the model object is not constructed at this point.
  • ServingTokenGeneratorSettings packages that factory with the resolved PipelineConfig, tokenizer, task, and memory plan. The handler passes this object to fastapi_app(settings, pipeline_settings) alongside server-level settings.
    • Settings contains server behavior such as exposed APIs, host, port, request limits, and queue limits. It comes from server flags and MAX_SERVE_* environment settings.
    • ServingTokenGeneratorSettings contains the resolved model-serving inputs: which factory to call, which config/tokenizer/task to use, and which memory plan was selected. fastapi_app() uses the server settings to configure routes and middleware, while its lifespan setup retains the serving settings to start and connect the model worker.
  • fastapi_config(app, server_settings=settings) converts the already-built FastAPI app and server settings into Uvicorn's Config. The same Settings object is passed again because this is a different job: fastapi_app() configures the ASGI application, while fastapi_config() reads host, port, and timeout values for the HTTP server.
  • Server(config) constructs Uvicorn's server object from that runtime config; construction does not start listening. The handler's serve() coroutine enters lifespan(...) first, then calls server.serve(...). During lifespan startup, start_model_worker(...) waits for the worker to become ready. In the worker, ModelWorker.run() invokes model_factory().

Why the guide says weight downloading happens later: “Later” means after the CLI has resolved the config, registry entry, tokenizer, and model factory. Some earlier metadata assets can already be read or fetched: AutoConfig loads config.json, the tokenizer may load vocabulary files, and generation defaults may load generation_config.json. The large model weight files are resolved when the worker invokes the factory and constructs TextGenerationPipeline. Its resolved_weight_paths() calls download_weight_files() for an online repo; that checks direct paths and the Hugging Face cache before downloading missing files. In the normal server path the worker reports ready before server.serve() begins accepting HTTP traffic, so weight loading is a startup step, not work deferred until the first request. The full weight path is traced in QnA 1.1.5.

QnA 1.1.3 · Tokenizer loadingHow does max serve reach AutoTokenizer?

Call-flow tree — from the resolved config to AutoTokenizer:

  • serve_api_server_and_model_worker() first builds PipelineConfig.from_args(), then calls PipelineRegistry.retrieve_factory() to prepare the model-serving components.
  • PipelineRegistry.architecture_for_config() resolves the checkpoint architecture name and task to the registered Llama declaration.
    • PipelineRegistry.retrieve_architecture() delegates the architecture lookup to ArchLookup.find() and ArchLookup.resolve().
  • llama_arch declares TextTokenizer as this architecture's tokenizer implementation.
    • At the selected-architecture call site, arch.tokenizer(...) constructs the tokenizer with the model path, Hugging Face revision, maximum length, and trust_remote_code setting.
    • TextTokenizer.__init__() creates MAX's tokenizer wrapper and delegates checkpoint tokenizer loading to AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(...). That Transformers call reads tokenizer files such as the vocabulary, tokenization rules, and special-token metadata. It uses the local Hub cache when possible and can fetch missing tokenizer assets at this preparation stage.
  • retrieve_factory() returns the tokenizer together with a deferred model factory and a memory plan. The serving handler stores those in ServingTokenGeneratorSettings; the worker later uses this tokenizer wrapper to encode prompts and decode generated token IDs.

Tokenizer loading is separate from model-weight loading and graph creation. The tokenizer may be fetched before the API server is assembled; the model factory loads the large tensor files during worker startup, as traced in QnA 1.1.5.

QnA 1.1.4 · Generation defaultsHow does GenerationConfig reach MAX sampling settings?

Call-flow tree — optional Hugging Face generation defaults to MAX sampling:

  • PipelineConfig.from_args() constructs the serving config and its main MAXModelConfig.from_pipeline_args().
  • _build_model_config() constructs the model config from the model path and resolved repository metadata.
    • During construction, MAXModelConfig._populate_generation_config() asks for the optional Hugging Face generation defaults when a model path is present.
    • MAXModelConfig._make_generation_config() calls GenerationConfig.from_pretrained(...) with the checkpoint repo, revision, and trust_remote_code setting. This reads an optional generation_config.json; the result is a Transformers GenerationConfig, not MAX's Llama3Config.
      • If the file is absent or loading raises, MAX logs at debug level and returns a default GenerationConfig from this same method.
  • The model config exposes the loaded values as sampling defaults. During PipelineConfig.from_args(), SamplingConfig.from_generation_config_sampling_defaults() combines supported defaults with the sampling fields the user explicitly set. The result determines the defaults the serving pipeline can honor.

This config is constructed before the model factory loads the large weight files. The argument manifest probe can create a temporary MAXModelConfig even before task inference; an inference prepass may create another instance. Each model-config instance can make its own generation-config load attempt, while the Hugging Face Hub cache may satisfy repeat file reads locally.

QnA 1.1.5 · Weight filesWhen are weight paths resolved, downloaded, and loaded?

Call-flow tree — when the large checkpoint weight files are resolved:

  • serve_api_server_and_model_worker() calls PipelineRegistry.retrieve_factory() after building the PipelineConfig.
  • retrieve_factory() resolves the registered architecture and memory plan, constructs the tokenizer, then packages a deferred pipeline constructor with functools.partial(...). It returns that factory; it has not called the factory or constructed the 7B model yet.
  • ServingTokenGeneratorSettings holds the factory and resolved pipeline config until serving startup. lifespan(...) calls start_model_worker(...) at this lifespan call site; it starts the worker process and waits for it to report ready.
    • ModelWorker.run() invokes model_factory(). This is when the deferred pipeline constructor runs, during server startup and before the API begins serving requests.
    • TextGenerationPipeline.__init__() sets up the session and asks the model config for local weight paths.
      • MAXModelConfig.resolved_weight_paths() uses a direct local path for a local checkpoint; for online Hugging Face weights it calls download_weight_files() at this MAX call site. The downloader checks direct paths and the Hugging Face cache first, then fetches missing files from the requested repo and revision. With header_only_weights, MAX takes a separate header-only path.
      • With the resolved paths, load_weights(weight_paths) returns a format-specific Weights provider; the pipeline invokes it at this call site. The Llama model consumes that provider in LlamaModelBase.load_graphs() and LlamaModelBase._load_state_dict(), followed by configuration finalization and graph construction in QnA 1.1.6.

The timing distinction is: Hugging Face config, tokenizer, and optional generation files can be accessed while the CLI prepares the pipeline; the large tensor files are resolved when the worker executes the model factory. For a warm cache or local checkpoint, download_weight_files() may perform no network download at all.

QnA 1.1.6 · Llama3Config lifecycleWhen are initialize and finalize called?

The registry's Llama declaration selects Llama3Config for MAX's architecture-specific model config. This is MAX's class; it is separate from the Transformers config returned by AutoConfig.

Call-flow tree — initialize() has setup uses; finalize() waits for the loaded weight state:

  • Memory planning, before the model factory runs:
  • PipelineRegistry.retrieve_factory() asks MemoryEstimator.plan() to estimate the model's memory needs before serving.
    • MemoryEstimator.plan() calls arch.config.initialize(...) with the pipeline/model config and sequence-length bound.
    • Llama3Config.initialize() reads the Hugging Face config and MAX settings to establish model dimensions and runtime choices needed for the plan. This call has no loaded model state dictionary to inspect.
  • Model construction, when the worker executes its factory:
  • ModelWorker.run() invokes model_factory(), which enters TextGenerationPipeline.__init__() and resolves weight paths inside that initializer before constructing the model.
    • The pipeline constructs Llama3Model. Its LlamaModelBase.__init__() runs through PipelineModelWithKVCache.__init__() to PipelineModel.__init__().
    • The base initializer calls model_config_cls.initialize(). Llama sets model_config_cls to Llama3Config in LlamaModelBase, so this is another config-only initialization point.
  • Weight-aware config finalization, before graph specs are compiled:
  • LlamaModelBase.load_model() enters LlamaModelBase.load_graphs().
    • LlamaModelBase._load_state_dict() obtains the model's state dictionary through PipelineModelWithKVCache._load_state_dict().
    • LlamaModelBase._create_model_config() delegates to LlamaModelBase._finalized_config().
    • _finalized_config() calls Llama3Config.initialize() to create the config object, then Llama3Config.finalize() with the Hugging Face config and loaded state dictionary.
      • Llama3Config.finalize() normalizes weight-name prefixes and derives weight-dependent settings such as quantization details and normalization dtype. It also uses checkpoint metadata such as tied-embedding settings.
    • With that config finalized, LlamaModelBase.graph_specs() chooses the single-device, tensor-parallel, or data-parallel graph spec. compile_and_init_graphs(...) is called at this Llama load site to build, compile, and initialize the selected graph(s).

Here Llama3Config.finalize() means finish the model's Python configuration using its weights. It is not Graph.output() finalization and not the compiler's device-graph finalize pass. Those graph/compiler stages happen after this config is ready.

The tokenizer and generation configuration are separate inputs to serving:

  • AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained() creates the Transformers tokenizer delegate used by MAX's TextTokenizer. It loads the vocabulary and tokenization rules so prompts become token IDs and generated IDs become text. It does not create the decoder graph.
  • GenerationConfig.from_pretrained() reads optional generation defaults such as max_length, temperature, and top_p. MAX maps supported defaults into its sampling configuration; explicit request sampling settings can take precedence. If loading the generation config fails, this path logs at debug level and uses a default Hugging Face GenerationConfig.

The architecture “database” is a set of Python dictionaries in process memory, owned by ArchLookup. The global PIPELINE_REGISTRY shares that lookup object.

Storage Key → value Lifetime / purpose
Hugging Face disk cache Repository + revision + filename → local file Reuse downloaded assets across runs
_lazy_architectures Architecture name → import instructions Describe how to load a built-in registration
architectures Architecture name → SupportedArchitecture object Reuse the imported description within the process
_architectures_by_task Architecture name + task → description Disambiguate architectures that share a name

The example_repo_ids in llama_arch are examples; the lookup key here is the architecture name. Checkpoint dimensions then become values in the selected config class.

3. When are architectures registered, and when is the model created?

The built-in mappings ship with MAX and are registered when Python imports max.pipelines. The matching architecture is imported on its first lookup. Creating a model instance happens later.

Stage Trigger What exists afterward
Create lookup objects Import the lookup and registry modules ARCH_LOOKUP and PIPELINE_REGISTRY share initially empty architecture tables
Record built-in mappings max.pipelines.__init__ calls register_all_models() Deferred mappings such as LlamaForCausalLM → .llama3 / llama_arch
Import the selected architecture First lookup of LlamaForCausalLM materialize() imports the package, reads llama_arch, and registers its SupportedArchitecture description
Construct the model The serving pipeline calls the selected pipeline_model class A Llama3Model instance receives configuration, weights, session, and devices; the graph-loading path follows

SOURCE — follow these exact locations:

  1. ARCH_LOOKUP = ArchLookup() and PIPELINE_REGISTRY = PipelineRegistry([], arch_lookup=ARCH_LOOKUP) create the shared lookup infrastructure.
  2. max.pipelines calls register_all_models(). Its registration loop records module, symbol, and package. A guard prevents repeated population.
  3. ArchLookup.materialize() calls importlib.import_module(), gets the declaration, and registers it.
  4. TextGenerationPipeline constructs the selected model using configuration and loaded weights.

A registration stores class references and model-loading metadata. It does not hold a loaded 7B model. Downloading another compatible checkpoint can reuse the same registration with different settings and tensors. Registration is separate from the graph finalization and compilation explained below.

This guide uses Llama 2 7B, one device, and the Graph API path. The working checkpoint name is meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf; a checkpoint revision and actual hardware run have not been captured. Hidden size, heads, vocabulary, and layer count are read from the checkpoint configuration rather than inferred from the name “7B.” The Graph API is the default when prefer_module_v3=False.

SOURCE — the initial serving route is serve_api_server_and_model_worker() → registry factory → model construction in TextGenerationPipeline. The model constructor calls load_model(), which selects the decoder returned by load_graphs() on this route.

255    def load_graphs(self, session: InferenceSession) -> dict[str, Model]:
256        """Compiles and initializes the graphs :meth:`graph_specs` returns.
257
258        Sets up the distributed runtime with ``_init_distributed_runtime``
259        first, since the graphs depend on it, and wires the batch processor
260        with ``_wire_batch_processor`` after.
261
262        Args:
263            session: The session that compiles and initializes the graphs.
264
265        Returns:
266            The initialized models, keyed by role.
267        """
268        state_dict = self._load_state_dict()
269        model_config = self._create_model_config(state_dict)
270        self._init_distributed_runtime(session, model_config)
271        with CompilationTimer("model") as timer:
272            specs = self.graph_specs(model_config)
273            timer.mark_build_complete()
274            self.compiled_modules = compile_and_init_graphs(session, specs)
275        models = {
276            role: compiled.engine_model
277            for role, compiled in self.compiled_modules.items()
278        }
279        self._maybe_release_host_weights(*models.values())
280        self._wire_batch_processor(models[GraphRole.DECODER], model_config)
281        return models

287    def graph_specs(self, model_config: Any) -> dict[str, GraphSpec]:
288        """Returns the decoder: data-parallel when the config asks for it,
289        else tensor-parallel across several devices, else single-device."""
290        assert isinstance(model_config, Llama3Config)
291        if model_config.data_parallel_degree > 1:
292            spec = self._data_parallel_spec(model_config)
293        elif len(self.devices) > 1:
294            spec = self._tensor_parallel_spec(model_config)
295        else:
296            spec = self._single_device_spec(model_config)
297        return {GraphRole.DECODER: spec}

Llama3Config.finalize() resolves settings that depend on checkpoint metadata: quantization, normalization, tied embeddings, stacked projections, and output policy. This mutates a Python configuration object. The symbolic graph has not been finalized by this call.

397    def finalize(
398        self,
399        huggingface_config: AutoConfig,
400        state_dict: dict[str, WeightData],
401        return_logits: ReturnLogits,
402        return_hidden_states: ReturnHiddenStates = ReturnHiddenStates.NONE,
403        norm_method: Literal["rms_norm", "layer_norm"] = "rms_norm",
404        attention_bias: bool = False,
405    ) -> None:
406        """Define parameters that can't be determined just from the pipeline config."""
407
408        # Normalize the LLM state dict so downstream introspection sees canonical
409        # Llama-style keys (no "language_model." or "model." prefix). This keeps
410        # float8 parsing and feature detection resilient to pack variations.
411        def _strip_prefix(s: str, prefix: str) -> str:
412            return s.removeprefix(prefix)
413
414        has_lm_prefix = any(k.startswith("language_model.") for k in state_dict)
415        has_model_prefix = any(k.startswith("model.") for k in state_dict)
416
417        if has_lm_prefix:
418            normalized_state_dict: dict[str, WeightData] = {
419                _strip_prefix(k, "language_model."): v
420                for k, v in state_dict.items()
421                if k.startswith("language_model.")
422            }
423        elif has_model_prefix:
424            normalized_state_dict = {
425                _strip_prefix(k, "model."): v
426                for k, v in state_dict.items()
427                if k.startswith("model.")
428            }
429        else:
430            normalized_state_dict = dict(state_dict)
431
432        quant_config = self._parse_quant_config(
433            huggingface_config, normalized_state_dict
434        )
435
436        # Determine norm_dtype.
437        # Note: due to automatic weight dtype casting, norm dtype is not always
438        # correct. To avoid any issue, only set norm_dtype for float8 models
439        # for now.
440        norm_dtype = None
441        if "layers.0.input_layernorm.weight" in normalized_state_dict:
442            norm_dtype = normalized_state_dict[
443                "layers.0.input_layernorm.weight"
444            ].dtype
445
446        # When tie_word_embeddings=True, the embedding weights are shared with
447        # the output weights.
448        if "tie_word_embeddings" in huggingface_config:
449            tie_word_embeddings = huggingface_config.tie_word_embeddings
450        else:
451            tie_word_embeddings = (
452                getattr(huggingface_config, "tie_word_embeddings", False)
453                or "lm_head.weight" not in normalized_state_dict
454            )
455
456        rms_norm_eps = None
457        if norm_method == "rms_norm":
458            rms_norm_eps = huggingface_config.rms_norm_eps
459
460        self.norm_method = norm_method
461        self.norm_dtype = norm_dtype
462        self.rms_norm_eps = rms_norm_eps
463        self.tie_word_embeddings = tie_word_embeddings
464        self.quant_config = quant_config
465        self.stacked_mlp = (
466            "layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj.weight" in normalized_state_dict
467        )
468        self.stacked_qkv = (
469            "layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight" in normalized_state_dict
470        )
471
472        self.attention_bias = attention_bias
473        self.return_logits = return_logits
474        self.return_hidden_states = return_hidden_states

Check your understanding: does the name Llama3Model hard-code a Llama 3 8B graph?

No. The registration selects this implementation, while the configuration supplies dimensions and model options. A specific checkpoint still needs compatible weights and settings; this source route is not a claim of a completed checkpoint run.

2. Record the computation

Tracing calls the Python model on symbolic graph inputs. The model's tensor operations append IR operations; they do not consume an actual prompt and generate tokens at this stage. Python construction and control flow still execute: the configured layer loop expands the decoder structure into the graph.

_single_device_spec() constructs the module, loads its weights, and captures its input contract. Weight values can exist before compilation. The later initialization step binds the named registry to the compiled engine model; these are different meanings of “loading weights.”

One block connects the model to the graph

SOURCE — the following diagram follows the ordinary residual path in TransformerBlock.__call__(). T is the packed token count and H is the configured hidden dimension. This is a shape/dataflow illustration.

tokens [T] -> embedding -> hidden states x [T,H]
                               |
                 +-------------+------------------+
                 |                                |
                 v                                |
             RMSNorm -> attention(Q/K/V, RoPE, KV) |
                 |                                |
                 +---------------------- add <----+
                                          |
                                          h [T,H]
                                          |
                         +----------------+----------------+
                         |                                 |
                         v                                 |
                     RMSNorm -> MLP ---------------------- add
                                                           |
                                                     next block

final block -> selected hidden-state rows -> norm -> LM head -> logits

The config chooses attention/linear/MLP implementations and the number of blocks. TransformerBlock exposes both residual paths. The full layer loop and logits postprocessing show how those blocks become a complete decoder.

92    def __init__(self, config: Llama3Config) -> None:
93        assert len(config.devices) == 1
94        self.config = config
95        rope = create_rope_embedding(
96            hidden_size=config.hidden_size,
97            num_attention_heads=config.num_attention_heads,
98            rope_theta=config.rope_theta,
99            max_seq_len=config.max_seq_len,
100            interleaved_rope_weights=config.interleaved_rope_weights,
101            rope_scaling_params=config.rope_scaling_params,
102            longrope_scaling_params=config.longrope_scaling_params,
103            device=config.devices[0],
104        )
105
106        # Select norm layer class.
107        create_norm: Callable[..., Module]
108        if config.norm_method == "rms_norm":
109            if config.rms_norm_eps is None:
110                raise ValueError(
111                    "rms_norm_eps cannot be None for model that uses RMSNorm."
112                )
113            create_norm = functools.partial(
114                RMSNorm,
115                config.hidden_size,
116                config.norm_dtype or config.dtype,
117                config.rms_norm_eps,
118                multiply_before_cast=False,  # disable Gemma3-style scaling
119            )
120        else:
121            create_norm = functools.partial(
122                ConstantLayerNorm,
123                config.hidden_size,
124                config.devices[0],
125                config.norm_dtype or config.dtype,
126            )
127
128        # Select linear layer class.
129        linear_cls: Callable[..., Linear]
130        if config.quantization_config:
131            linear_cls = functools.partial(
132                GPTQLinear, quantization_config=config.quantization_config
133            )
134        else:
135            linear_cls = functools.partial(
136                Linear, quant_config=config.quant_config
137            )
138        if config.stacked_mlp and config.quant_config:
139            raise ValueError(
140                "StackedMLP and scaled quantization are not compatible"
141            )
142        mlp_cls = (
143            StackedMLP
144            if config.stacked_mlp
145            else functools.partial(MLP, quant_config=config.quant_config)
146        )
147        attention_cls: Callable[..., AttentionWithRope]
148        if config.model_quantization_encoding == QuantizationEncoding.GPTQ:
149            assert config.quantization_config is not None
150            assert not config.attention_bias, (
151                "Attention bias is not supported for GPTQAttentionWithRope."
152            )
153            attention_cls = functools.partial(
154                GPTQAttentionWithRope,
155                quantization_config=config.quantization_config,
156                scale=config.attention_multiplier,
157            )
158        elif config.model_quantization_encoding is not None:
159            assert not config.attention_bias, (
160                "Attention bias is not supported for GGUFQAttentionWithRope."
161            )
162            attention_cls = functools.partial(
163                GGUFQAttentionWithRope,
164                quantization_encoding=config.model_quantization_encoding,
165                scale=config.attention_multiplier,
166            )
167        else:
168            attention_cls = functools.partial(
169                AttentionWithRope,
170                stacked_qkv=config.stacked_qkv,
171                scale=config.attention_multiplier,
172                clip_qkv=config.clip_qkv,
173                has_bias=config.attention_bias,
174                quant_config=config.quant_config,
175            )
176
177        layers = [
178            TransformerBlock(
179                attention=attention_cls(
180                    num_attention_heads=config.num_attention_heads,
181                    num_key_value_heads=config.num_key_value_heads,
182                    hidden_size=config.hidden_size,
183                    kv_params=config.kv_params,
184                    dtype=config.dtype,
185                    rope=rope,
186                    linear_cls=linear_cls,
187                    devices=config.devices,
188                ),
189                mlp=mlp_cls(
190                    config.dtype,
191                    config.model_quantization_encoding,
192                    config.hidden_size,
193                    config.intermediate_size,
194                    config.devices,
195                    linear_cls,
196                ),
197                attention_norm=create_norm(),
198                mlp_norm=create_norm(),
199                residual_multiplier=config.residual_multiplier,
200            )
201            for i in range(config.num_hidden_layers)
202        ]
203
204        # Create Embedding and output layers.
205        embedding_output_dtype = config.dtype
206        embedding_output_quantization = config.model_quantization_encoding
207        if config.model_quantization_encoding == QuantizationEncoding.GPTQ:
208            embedding_output_dtype = DType.bfloat16
209            embedding_output_quantization = None
210        if config.quant_config and config.quant_config.embedding_output_dtype:
211            embedding_output_dtype = config.quant_config.embedding_output_dtype
212        embedding_layer = Embedding(
213            config.vocab_size,
214            config.hidden_size,
215            embedding_output_dtype,
216            config.devices[0],
217            quantization_encoding=embedding_output_quantization,
218        )
219        output = Linear(
220            config.hidden_size,
221            config.vocab_size,
222            embedding_output_dtype,
223            config.devices[0],
224            quantization_encoding=embedding_output_quantization,
225        )
226
227        if config.tie_word_embeddings:
228            output.set_shared_weight("weight", embedding_layer.weight)
229
230        super().__init__(
231            dim=config.hidden_size,
232            n_heads=config.num_attention_heads,
233            layers=layers,
234            norm=create_norm(),
235            output=output,
236            embedding=embedding_layer,
237            kv_params=config.kv_params,
238            rope=rope,
239            return_logits=config.return_logits,
240            return_hidden_states=config.return_hidden_states,
241            embedding_multiplier=config.embedding_multiplier,
242            logits_scaling=config.logits_scaling,
243            target_layer_ids=config.target_layer_ids,
244        )

TransformerBlock.__call__Record the attention and MLP residual paths for one decoder block.SOURCE28 lines
max/python/max/nn/transformer/transformer.pyL293–L320 · 610f7111836d
Download fileLink to cell
293    def __call__(
294        self,
295        layer_idx: TensorValue,
296        x: TensorValue,
297        kv_collection: PagedCacheValues,
298        freqs_cis: TensorValue,
299        input_row_offsets: TensorValue,
300    ) -> TensorValue:
301        residual_multiplier = ops.constant(
302            self.residual_multiplier, x.dtype, device=x.device
303        )
304        attn_out = self.self_attn(
305            layer_idx,
306            self.input_layernorm(x),
307            kv_collection,
308            freqs_cis=freqs_cis,
309            input_row_offsets=input_row_offsets,
310        )
311
312        if self.residual_multiplier != 1.0:
313            attn_out = attn_out * residual_multiplier
314
315        h = x + attn_out
316        mlp = self.mlp(self.post_attention_layernorm(h))
317        if self.residual_multiplier != 1.0:
318            mlp = mlp * residual_multiplier
319
320        return h + mlp

618        self,

Download fileLink to cell
413def logits_postprocess(
414    h: TensorValue,
415    input_row_offsets: TensorValue,
416    return_n_logits: TensorValue,
417    norm: Callable[[TensorValue], TensorValue],
418    lm_head: Callable[[TensorValue], TensorValue],
419    return_logits: ReturnLogits,
420    return_hidden_states: ReturnHiddenStates = ReturnHiddenStates.NONE,
421    logits_scaling: float = 1.0,
422    capture_hidden_states: list[list[TensorValue]] | None = None,
423) -> DecoderOutputs:
424    """Performs common logits postprocessing for single-device models.
425
426    Handles last-token gathering, logits computation, optional logits
427    scaling, and hidden states return.
428
429    Args:
430        h: The hidden states from the final transformer layer.
431        input_row_offsets: The row offsets for ragged batching.
432        return_n_logits: The number of logits to return per sequence.
433        norm: The normalization function applied before the language model head.
434        lm_head: The language model head projection.
435        return_logits: Which logits to return.
436        return_hidden_states: Which hidden states to return. Defaults to
437            ``ReturnHiddenStates.NONE``.
438        logits_scaling: A divisor applied to logits after projection. Logits
439            are divided by this value before returning. Defaults to ``1.0``
440            (no scaling).
441        capture_hidden_states: For ``SELECTED_LAYERS`` mode, the
442            per-layer captured hidden states gathered during the layer loop.
443            See :func:`extract_hs`.
444
445    Returns:
446        The named outputs; see :func:`logits_outputs`.
447    """
448    last_h = ops.gather(h, input_row_offsets[1:] - 1, axis=0)
449    last_logits = ops.cast(lm_head(norm(last_h)), DType.float32)
450    logits = None
451    offsets = None
452
453    if return_logits == ReturnLogits.VARIABLE:
454        return_n_logits_range = ops.range(
455            return_n_logits[0],
456            0,
457            -1,
458            out_dim="return_n_logits_range",
459            device=h.device,
460            dtype=DType.int64,
461        )
462        offsets = (
463            ops.unsqueeze(input_row_offsets[1:], -1) - return_n_logits_range
464        )
465        last_indices = ops.reshape(offsets, shape=(-1,))
466        last_tokens = ops.gather(h, last_indices, axis=0)
467        logits = ops.cast(lm_head(norm(last_tokens)), DType.float32)
468        offsets = ops.range(
469            0,
470            TensorValue(last_indices.shape[0]) + return_n_logits[0],
471            return_n_logits[0],
472            out_dim="logit_offsets",
473            device=h.device,
474            dtype=DType.int64,
475        )
476    elif return_logits == ReturnLogits.ALL:
477        logits = ops.cast(lm_head(norm(h)), DType.float32)
478        offsets = input_row_offsets
479
480    if logits_scaling != 1.0:
481        last_logits = last_logits / logits_scaling
482        if logits is not None:
483            logits = logits / logits_scaling
484
485    return logits_outputs(
486        last_logits,
487        logits,
488        offsets,
489        return_hidden_states,
490        extract_hs(
491            return_hidden_states=return_hidden_states,
492            last_token_hs_distributed=[last_h],
493            all_hs_distributed=[h],
494            normalizer=[norm],
495            capture_hidden_states=capture_hidden_states,
496        ),
497    )

Symbolic inputs describe a call boundary

Input Declared type / placement Meaning
tokens int64[total_seq_len], selected device All tokens packed into one sequence buffer
row_offsets uint32[input_row_offsets_len], selected device Boundaries between sequences; conventionally B+1 entries for B sequences
return_n_logits int64[return_n_logits], CPU Count input used by the configured variable-logits path
KV subtree Types from kv_params.get_symbolic_inputs() Cache buffers and metadata consumed by attention

Those are symbolic type declarations. Actual buffer values, their concrete lengths, and the cache contents arrive during execution. The graph's fixed architecture dimensions and its variable batch/token dimensions serve different purposes.

539def ragged_batch_inputs(
540    device_ref: DeviceRef,
541    fields: Sequence[str] = ("tokens", "row_offsets", "return_n_logits"),
542    *,
543    data_parallel_degree: int = 1,
544    hidden_states: tuple[DType, int] | None = None,
545    row_offsets_devices: Sequence[DeviceRef] | None = None,
546) -> RaggedBatch:
547    """Returns the named per-batch graph inputs, in the order ``fields`` gives.
548
549    Args:
550        device_ref: The device that holds the token and row-offset tensors.
551        fields: The inputs to include, in graph order. Any of ``tokens``,
552            ``row_offsets``, ``host_row_offsets``, ``return_n_logits``,
553            ``data_parallel_splits`` and ``hidden_states``.
554        data_parallel_degree: The number of replicas, which sizes
555            ``data_parallel_splits``.
556        hidden_states: The ``(dtype, hidden_size)`` of the EAGLE draft's
557            hidden-state input. Required when ``fields`` names
558            ``hidden_states``.
559        row_offsets_devices: The devices that each take their own
560            ``row_offsets``, for a graph that does not broadcast them.
561            ``row_offsets`` is then a tuple with one type per device.
562
563    Returns:
564        The input types keyed by field name.
565    """
566    available: dict[str, TensorType | tuple[TensorType, ...]] = {
567        "tokens": TensorType(
568            DType.int64, shape=["total_seq_len"], device=device_ref
569        ),
570        "row_offsets": TensorType(
571            DType.uint32, shape=["input_row_offsets_len"], device=device_ref
572        ),
573        "host_row_offsets": TensorType(
574            DType.uint32,
575            shape=["input_row_offsets_len"],
576            device=DeviceRef.CPU(),
577        ),
578        "return_n_logits": TensorType(
579            DType.int64, shape=["return_n_logits"], device=DeviceRef.CPU()
580        ),
581        "data_parallel_splits": TensorType(
582            DType.int64,
583            shape=[data_parallel_degree + 1],
584            device=DeviceRef.CPU(),
585        ),
586    }
587    if row_offsets_devices is not None:
588        available["row_offsets"] = tuple(
589            TensorType(
590                DType.uint32, shape=["input_row_offsets_len"], device=device
591            )
592            for device in row_offsets_devices
593        )
594    if hidden_states is not None:
595        dtype, hidden_size = hidden_states
596        available["hidden_states"] = TensorType(
597            dtype, shape=["total_seq_len", hidden_size], device=device_ref
598        )
599    return RaggedBatch((name, available[name]) for name in fields)

GraphSpec.trace()
  -> flatten named input types
  -> Llama3.trace()
     -> define forward adapter for flat inputs and KV reconstruction
     -> Graph(name, forward, input_types=...)
        -> create MLIR module and mo.graph input arguments
        -> forward(*graph.inputs)
        -> Graph.output(returned_values)

Llama3.trace() reconstructs the nested KV collection from flat graph inputs. Graph.__init__() creates the graph container and its initially empty result list. Passing forward causes automatic tracing and output finalization. The graph body can initially contain RMO operations; early compiler processing legalizes them. The container name mo.graph does not mean every initial operation belongs to the MO dialect.

Check your understanding: what is executing when the Python layer loop runs during tracing?

Python is constructing the symbolic computation. Graph tensor operations record dataflow on symbolic values. Runtime token buffers are supplied to the initialized engine model later. Some host-side setup work can occur during construction; tracing is not equivalent to running Llama inference.

3. Finalize the graph

Graph.output() completes the graph's output contract and verifies its IR. The Llama path reaches it automatically from the Graph constructor after the symbolic forward returns. There is no separate Python Graph.finalize() call on this route.

Three different objects can be “finalized”

Name Object Meaning
Llama3Config.finalize() Python model configuration Resolve checkpoint-dependent settings before tracing
Graph.output() Symbolic graph Install output types, signature, terminator, and names; verify graph IR
FinalizeDeviceGraphsPass Marked MGP device-graph model Finish device-graph collective construction during native compilation

1396    def output(self, *outputs: GraphOutputs) -> None:
1397        """Sets the output values of the graph and finalizes construction.
1398
1399        Call this once after building all ops. The graph can't be executed
1400        until ``output()`` has been called. Subsequent calls to
1401        :attr:`output_types` read back the types of the values passed here.
1402
1403        For example, build a graph that doubles its input and set the
1404        output:
1405
1406        .. code-block:: python
1407
1408            from max.dtype import DType
1409            from max.graph import DeviceRef, Graph, ops
1410            from max.graph.type import TensorType
1411
1412            input_type = TensorType(DType.float32, [4], DeviceRef.CPU())
1413
1414            with Graph("double", input_types=[input_type]) as graph:
1415                x = graph.inputs[0].tensor
1416                two = ops.constant(2.0, DType.float32, device=DeviceRef.CPU())
1417                graph.output(ops.elementwise.mul(x, two))
1418
1419        Pass one named tree, such as a dict of logits and hidden states, to
1420        name each output by its path in it; :attr:`output_tree` then returns
1421        the output types in that structure.
1422
1423        Args:
1424            outputs: The output values of the graph, or a single tree whose
1425                leaves they are. Each value may be a :class:`Value` or any
1426                :class:`~max.graph.TensorValueLike`.
1427        """
1428        root = (
1429            outputs[0]
1430            if len(outputs) == 1 and tree.is_node(outputs[0])
1431            else outputs
1432        )
1433        leaves, self._output_structure = tree.flatten(root)
1434        if any(isinstance(leaf, str) for leaf in leaves):
1435            raise TypeError(
1436                f"graph outputs {leaves} include a string, as when a named"
1437                " tree is unpacked into its keys: pass the tree itself, as"
1438                " graph.output(outputs)"
1439            )
1440        outputs = tuple(
1441            o if isinstance(o, Value) else TensorValue(o) for o in leaves
1442        )
1443        outputs = cast(tuple[Value[Any], ...], outputs)
1444        # mo.output doesn't support infer_type
1445        graph_body_args = self._graph_body.arguments
1446        output_values: list[Value[Any]] = list(outputs)
1447        if self._has_chain_input:
1448            output_values = self.device_chains.pack(output_values)
1449        mlir_values: list[_Value[Any]] = [v._mlir_value for v in output_values]
1450
1451        # We have a type mismatch now, these are MLIR types
1452        # Convert from max._core.Type to mlir.Type using CAPI bridge
1453        output_types = [
1454            mlir.Type._CAPICreate(value.type._CAPIPtr)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
1455            for value in mlir_values
1456        ]
1457
1458        # Need to set some more stuff.
1459        function_type = mlir.FunctionType.get(
1460            graph_body_args.types,
1461            output_types,
1462        )
1463        signature = mlir.Type.parse(f"!kgen.generator<{function_type}>")
1464        self._mlir_op.attributes["signature"] = mlir.TypeAttr.get(signature)
1465        self._mlir_op.attributes["functionType"] = mlir.TypeAttr.get(
1466            function_type
1467        )
1468
1469        self._add_op_generated(
1470            _mo.OutputOp,
1471            mlir_values,
1472            _kgen.ParameterExprArrayAttr([]),
1473            attach_profile_scopes=False,
1474        )
1475
1476        # Set the result_names metadata on the staged op, which is needed by
1477        # the engine for execution.
1478        # Note that result_names here needs to match kMgpModelResultNames.
1479        input_names = [f'"input{i}"' for i in range(len(self.inputs))]
1480        self._mlir_op.attributes["argument_names"] = mlir.Attribute.parse(
1481            f"[{', '.join(input_names)}]"
1482        )
1483        output_names = [f'"output{i}"' for i in range(len(output_types))]
1484        self._mlir_op.attributes["result_names"] = mlir.Attribute.parse(
1485            f"[{', '.join(output_names)}]"
1486        )
1487
1488        self._subgraphs = {}
1489        # Outputting means the graph is complete. Verify the entire graph.
1490        try:
1491            with self._capturing_mlir_diagnostics():
1492                assert self._mlir_op.verify()
1493        except Exception as e:
1494            print(self)
1495            raise ValueError(
1496                "Graph failed to verify. Please file an issue. This should be"
1497                " impossible." + f"\n{e}"
1498            ) from None

What the completed contract provides

  • Output structure: Python retains a tree describing semantic groups such as logits and hidden states, while the engine boundary uses flat values.
  • Types: functionType and signature describe actual graph argument and result types. Symbolic dimensions are allowed to remain symbolic.
  • Termination: mo.output identifies the SSA values returned by the graph.
  • Names: engine metadata uses ordinal names such as input0 and output0.
  • Verification: _mlir_op.verify() checks the completed graph. Compiler legality, weight-buffer validation, and numerical correctness require their corresponding later checks.

Context exit has a separate job

The with graph: context chooses where operations are recorded. Graph.__exit__() unwinds that context through _enter() and restores the previous CURRENT_GRAPH. Compilation starts through a later session call.

4. Cross into the compiler

The compiled object is produced by the session, after the graph is traced. compile_and_init_graphs() makes the order explicit: trace → compile or reuse → gather named weights → initialize. It also retains the input/output tree information needed by the serving wrapper.

183def compile_and_init_graphs(
184    session: InferenceSession, specs: Mapping[str, GraphSpec]
185) -> dict[str, CompiledCallable[..., Any]]:
186    """Compiles and initializes each role's graph.
187
188    Roles that share a group trace into one :class:`~max.graph.Module`,
189    compile once, and initialize once with the weights of all of them; each
190    role's callable then holds the same compiled model. Each compiles through
191    :meth:`~max.engine.InferenceSession.compile_reusing_mefs`, so an ungrouped
192    role reuses the session's precompiled or exported MEFs. A group compiles
193    every time, as any module of several graphs does. Inside
194    :func:`compile_roles_separately`, groups are ignored.
195
196    Each callable is called with one argument per input type, positionally,
197    or with the named input tree as its one argument, and returns the graph's
198    outputs in the tree its ``forward`` returned. It keeps no weight registry,
199    so the host weights can be released after initialization. A ModuleV3
200    role's callable instead takes and returns what the module's ``forward``
201    does, adds the signal buffers a multi-device graph takes, and keeps its
202    weight registry.
203
204    Args:
205        session: The session that compiles and initializes the graphs.
206        specs: The graphs to compile, keyed by role.
207
208    Returns:
209        Each role's compiled, initialized graph.
210
211    Raises:
212        ValueError: If two roles in one group share a graph name, or bind
213            different values to one weight name.
214    """
215    separately = _compile_roles_separately.get()
216    groups: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
217    for role, spec in specs.items():
218        # Ungrouped roles compile alone, so each gets its own key.
219        key = (
220            spec.group
221            if spec.group is not None and not separately
222            else f"\0{role}"
223        )
224        groups.setdefault(key, []).append(role)
225
226    callables: dict[str, CompiledCallable[..., Any]] = {}
227    for members in groups.values():
228        names = [specs[role].name for role in members]
229        if len(set(names)) != len(names):
230            raise ValueError(
231                f"roles {members} share a group but not distinct graph names:"
232                f" {names}"
233            )
234        traced_graph: Graph | GraphModule
235        if len(members) == 1:
236            graphs = {members[0]: specs[members[0]].trace()}
237            traced_graph = graphs[members[0]]
238            extensions = None
239        else:
240            traced_graph = GraphModule()
241            graphs = {role: specs[role].trace(traced_graph) for role in members}
242            # A graph carries its own extensions; a module of graphs does not.
243            extensions = [
244                path
245                for role in members
246                for path in specs[role].custom_extensions
247            ]
248        output_trees = {
249            role: graph.output_tree for role, graph in graphs.items()
250        }
251        # Not session.load_all, which drops the compiled model a callable
252        # keeps to export its MEF.
253        compiled = session.compile_reusing_mefs(
254            traced_graph, custom_extensions=extensions
255        )
256
257        weights: dict[str, DLPackArray] = {}
258        for role in members:
259            for name, value in specs[role].weights_registry().items():
260                if weights.setdefault(name, value) is not value:
261                    raise ValueError(
262                        f"weight {name!r} has two different values"
263                    )
264        by_name = session.init_all(compiled, weights_registry=weights)
265        for role in members:
266            if len(by_name) == 1:
267                # The session can hand back a cached MEF compiled from an
268                # identical graph under another name, so don't look it up by
269                # this spec's name.
270                (model,) = by_name.values()
271            else:
272                model = by_name[specs[role].name]
273            spec = specs[role]
274            if isinstance(spec.module, ModuleV3):
275                # The trace's own signature, so the callable takes and
276                # returns what ``forward`` does and adds any signal buffers.
277                staged, registry = spec._staged
278                callables[role] = CompiledCallable.from_engine_model(
279                    staged, compiled, model, registry
280                )
281            else:
282                callables[role] = _callable(
283                    compiled, model, spec.input_types, output_trees[role]
284                )
285                _check_inputs(role, callables[role].in_tree)
286                _check_outputs(role, callables[role].out_tree)
287    return callables

Follow the payload, not just the function names

Boundary Payload Result
Pipeline → Python session Completed Graph/Module, extensions CompiledModel handle
Python → C++ session MLIR module capsule, pipeline name, options Native asynchronous compilation result
C++ session → engine CompilationRequest CPU worker scheduled to process it
Engine → frontend Source pointer, format, settings Compiled MEF buffer or cached MEF
Frontend → compiler Cloned MLIR module and pipeline options Lowered module, then MEF serialization
MEF reader → session Parsed compiled-model objects Artifact available for initialization

The native compile handoffs

Portable call sequence
Pipeline      Python session    C++ session    Engine worker   CompiledModels   MOF frontend   Compiler
   |                |                |              |                |               |             |
   | compile(graph) |                |              |                |               |             |
   |--------------->| capsule        |              |                |               |             |
   |                |--------------->| request      |                |               |             |
   |                |                |------------->| create         |               |             |
   |                |                |              |--------------->| compile       |             |
   |                |                |              |                |-------------->| run passes  |
   |                |                |              |                |               |------------>|
   |                |                |              |                |               |<------------|
   |                |                |              |                |<--------------| MEF buffer  |
   |                |                |              |<---------------| read artifact |             |
   |                |<----------------------------------------------- compiled result              |
   |<---------------| wait complete  |              |                |               |             |
   | init_all(weights)              |              |                |               |             |
   |--------------->| native initialization -> executable models    |               |             |

GraphSpec.trace / Graph.output finish before this cold compilation sequence.
The engine schedules the compile on a CPU worker; arrows show call/result order.

The native implementations are present in this checkout. The Python/C++ crossing is a visible language boundary, not an unexplained stop in the source trail.

Python session: dispatch, handoff, and wait

compile_reusing_mefs() may resolve a stored artifact. Otherwise compile_async() selects a path or in-memory graph. For a Graph, it collects expected weight-device metadata and seeds kernel declarations before _compile_module() passes the MLIR capsule into C++.

The process-wide compilation lock spans the asynchronous compile. A completion callback releases it. The synchronous compile() waits on the result and surfaces errors before returning the artifact.

931            RuntimeError: If reusing and no recorded artifact matches
932                ``model``'s name and signature.
933        """
934        # See `_precompiled_mefs` for why a caller would want this: it lets the
935        # compile happen somewhere that holds no accelerator.
936        store = (
937            self._mef_store
938            if self._mef_store is not None
939            else InferenceSession.default_mef_store
940        )
941        if store is None or not isinstance(model, Graph):
942            return self.compile(
943                model,
944                custom_extensions=custom_extensions,
945                tile_based_fusion=tile_based_fusion,
946            )
947
948        if not store.exporting:
949            artifact = store.claim_import(model)
950            # A store with nothing to say about this graph declines it, and
951            # the compile happens here as it would with no store at all.
952            if artifact is not None:
953                return self.compile(artifact)
954            return self.compile(
955                model,
956                custom_extensions=custom_extensions,
957                tile_based_fusion=tile_based_fusion,
958            )
959
960        compiled = self.compile(
961            model,
962            custom_extensions=custom_extensions,
963            tile_based_fusion=tile_based_fusion,
964        )
965        compiled.export_mef(store.claim_export(model))
966        store.write_manifest()
967        return compiled

969    def compile_async(
970        self,
971        model: str | Path | Module | Graph,
972        *,
973        custom_extensions: CustomExtensionsType | None = None,
974        tile_based_fusion: bool = False,
975    ) -> CompiledModel:
976        """Compiles a model without blocking on the compilation finishing.
977
978        Returns as soon as the compile is scheduled; the returned
979        :class:`CompiledModel` wraps a pending compilation that runs on the
980        runtime's worker pool. Compilation errors are not raised here — they
981        surface when the artifact is awaited, for example by :meth:`init`,
982        :meth:`init_all`, or :meth:`CompiledModel.export_mef`. Use
983        :meth:`compile` for the synchronous variant that blocks and raises.
984
985        Compiles are serialized process-wide: if another compile is in
986        flight (from any session), this call blocks until it resolves
987        before scheduling this one.
988
989        Args:
990            model: A :class:`Graph` instance, a :class:`max.graph.Module`
991                containing one or more ``mo.graph`` ops, or the path to a
992                saved model file (for example, a ``.mef`` file).
993
994            custom_extensions: The extensions to load for the model.
995                Supports paths to ``.mojoc`` custom ops.
996
997            tile_based_fusion: When ``True``, compile the graph under the tile-based
998                programming model, in which the graph compiler selects
999                tile-based kernels (operating on ``TileTensor`` values instead
1000                of SIMD). Only applies when ``model`` is a :class:`Graph` or
1001                :class:`max.graph.Module`; ignored for precompiled ``.mef``
1002                paths. Defaults to ``False``.
1003
1004        Returns:
1005            A :class:`CompiledModel` artifact wrapping the pending compilation.
1006        """
1007        custom_extensions_final: list[CustomExtensionType] = []
1008        if custom_extensions is not None:
1009            custom_extensions_final = _process_custom_extensions_objects(
1010                custom_extensions
1011            )
1012
1013        # Track the MLIR module if we have one so we can enumerate graph
1014        # names and capture expected-weight metadata for init-time validation.
1015        module: Module | None = None
1016        expected_weights: dict[str, Any] | None = None
1017
1018        if isinstance(model, Path | str):
1019            handle = self._impl.compile(model, custom_extensions_final)
1020        elif isinstance(model, Graph):
1021            module = model.module
1022            custom_extensions_final.extend(
1023                _process_custom_extensions_objects(model.kernel_libraries_paths)
1024            )
1025
1026            # TODO: if the model has been loaded from a serialized MLIR
1027            # file, we don't have the _weights attribute available to us
1028            if hasattr(model, "_weights"):
1029                expected_weights = {
1030                    name: weight.value.device
1031                    for name, weight in model._weights.items()
1032                }
1033
1034            # Seed the model module with kernel decls + the opaque-type
1035            # mapping from the graph's KernelLibrary. The GC pipeline
1036            # detects the mapping attribute and skips
1037            # `mogg-import-packages`, so the expensive package-loading
1038            # step (run once at KernelLibrary construction) doesn't
1039            # repeat on every compile.
1040            kernel_library = getattr(model, "_kernel_library", None)
1041            if kernel_library is not None:
1042                kernel_library._analysis.seed_kernel_decls(module.mlir_module)
1043
1044            handle = self._compile_module(
1045                module, custom_extensions_final, tile_based_fusion
1046            )
1047        elif isinstance(model, Module):
1048            module = model
1049            handle = self._compile_module(
1050                module, custom_extensions_final, tile_based_fusion
1051            )
1052        else:
1053            raise RuntimeError("The model is not a valid path or module.")
1054
1055        compiled = CompiledModel(
1056            compiled=handle, expected_weights=expected_weights
1057        )
1058        if module is not None:
1059            compiled._graph_names = tuple(module.top_level_graph_names())
1060        return compiled

1276    def _compile_module(
1277        self,
1278        module: Module,
1279        custom_extensions_final: list[CustomExtensionType],
1280        tile_based_fusion: bool = False,
1281    ) -> _AsyncValue[_CompiledModels]:
1282        """Compiles an MLIR module under the process-global compilation lock.
1283
1284        Compilation itself is asynchronous; a compile failure surfaces when
1285        the returned value is awaited (see :meth:`compile`).
1286
1287        Raises:
1288            RuntimeError: If synchronous compile setup fails; the message
1289                points at the ``max-debug.source-tracebacks`` config key
1290                for richer diagnostics.
1291        """
1292        _COMPILATION_LOCK.acquire()
1293        try:
1294            handle = self._impl.compile(
1295                module.mlir_module._CAPIPtr,
1296                custom_extensions_final,
1297                _derive_pipeline_name(module),
1298                tile_based_fusion,
1299            )
1300        except Exception as e:
1301            _COMPILATION_LOCK.release()
1302            raise RuntimeError(self._compile_failure_message()) from e
1303        # Released from a runtime worker thread when the compile resolves.
1304        handle.add_done_callback(lambda _: _COMPILATION_LOCK.release())
1305        return handle

1104            compiled = self.compile_async(
1105                model,
1106                custom_extensions=custom_extensions,
1107                tile_based_fusion=tile_based_fusion,
1108            )

1121        # failure.

C++ session and engine

The C++ session turns the capsule into a CompilationRequest with an opaque source pointer and format. Engine::Context::compileModel() schedules a CPU task. That task calls compileModelSync(), which supplies device configuration and calls CompiledModels::create().

654AsyncRT::AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels> M::Core::InferenceSession::compile(
655    const nb::capsule &model,
656    std::vector<std::filesystem::path> &&customExtensions,
657    std::string &&pipelineName, bool tileBasedFusion) {
658  CompilationRequest compileConfig =
659      populateCompileConfig(std::move(customExtensions));
660  // Set pipeline name. Tracked for telemetry.
661  compileConfig.setPipelineName(std::move(pipelineName));
662  // Opt into the tile-based programming model if requested.
663  compileConfig.setTileBasedFusion(tileBasedFusion);
664  // When the format is Max Graph, model is a opaque pointer of graph.
665  // So we cast it to a pointer representation and pass it along.
666  // The C API will open appropriate dylib for the format and pass the
667  // pointer to the library. We have to make sure the pointer is passed down
668  // to the library which created the pointer. This is to ensure mlir type
669  // id invariants are not broken.
670  compileConfig.setModelSource(ModelSource{
671      .source = model.data(),
672      .fileFormat = frameworkToFileFormat(),
673  });
674  // Compile async, so it's safe to hold the gil here
675  AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels> asyncModel =
676      compileModel(*runtimeContext, std::move(compileConfig));
677  return asyncModel;
678}

Frontend and compiled artifact

For a graph source, CompiledModels::create() constructs the MOF frontend, calls compileToBinary(), and reads its returned MEF. For an already compiled MEF path, it reads the artifact directly.

The frontend clones the source module before applying compiler transformations, resolves options, and checks the native MEF cache. A miss enters convertMOToMEF(): run the compiler, then serialize MGP to MEF.

101CompiledModels::create(M::ContextRef context, const CompilationRequest &compCfg,
102                       const M::Engine::Config &rtCfg) {
103  // If model is from an opaque source with a known format.
104  if (auto modelSourceOr = compCfg.getModelSource(); modelSourceOr) {
105    auto modelSource = modelSourceOr.value();
106    auto frameworkCtxOr = setupFrameworkContext(context.copy(), compCfg, rtCfg);
107    if (frameworkCtxOr.isError())
108      return frameworkCtxOr.takeError();
109    std::unique_ptr<MOFContext> &frameworkCtx = *frameworkCtxOr;
110
111    auto outputBufferOr = frameworkCtx->compileToBinary(modelSource.source,
112                                                        modelSource.fileFormat);
113    if (outputBufferOr.isError())
114      return outputBufferOr.takeError();
115
116    BufferRef outputBuffer = outputBufferOr.takeValue();
117
118    return read(std::move(outputBuffer), std::move(frameworkCtx),
119                SourceModel(modelSource));
120  } else if (auto modelPathOr = compCfg.getModelPath(); modelPathOr) {
121    // Capture runtime configuration which is also needed by the compile-time
122    // configuration, since that's currently the only way to convey options
123    // down into the driver's M_compileToBinary.
124    auto modelPath = modelPathOr.value();
125
126    ErrorOr<ModelContext> modelCtxOr =
127        loadModelFramework(modelPath, context.copy());
128    if (modelCtxOr.isError())
129      return modelCtxOr.takeError();
130    auto modelCtx = modelCtxOr.takeValue();
131    // Convey compilation options to the driver.
132    ErrorOrSuccess errorOr =
133        setModelAndFramework(context.copy(), modelCtx, compCfg, rtCfg);
134    if (errorOr.isError())
135      return errorOr.takeError();
136
137    SourceModel &sourceModel = modelCtx.model;
138    M::BufferRef modelBuffer = modelCtx.buffer.copy();
139    std::unique_ptr<MOFContext> &frameworkCtx = modelCtx.frameworkCtx;
140
141    // If it's already compiled use that directly.
142    if (modelCtx.model.format() == FileFormat::kMEFFile) {
143      return read(modelBuffer.copy(), std::move(frameworkCtx), modelCtx.model);
144    }
145
146    // Actually compile the model.
147    auto outputBufferOr =
148        frameworkCtx->compileToBinary(modelBuffer.copy(), sourceModel.format());
149    if (outputBufferOr.isError())
150      return outputBufferOr.takeError();
151
152    BufferRef outputBuffer = outputBufferOr.takeValue();
153    return read(std::move(outputBuffer), std::move(frameworkCtx),
154                modelCtx.model);
155  }
156  auto error = Error("Model path or source is not set in compilation config");
157  auto *ctx = context->get<GML::MaxEngineTelemetryContext>();
158  GML::emitErrorTelemetry<GML::MaxEngineErrorCode::UserInputError>(
159      *ctx, error.copy());
160  return error;
161}
