377M::ErrorOr<M::BufferRef> MOFContext::compileToBinary(void *source,
378                                                     FileFormat format) {
379  // Cheap: weights are dense_resource attributes owned by the MLIRContext.
380  OwningOpRef<ModuleOp> moduleOp =
381      ModuleOp::getFromOpaquePointer(source).clone();
382
383  auto &maxContext = impl->maxContext;
384  MLIRContext *mlirCtx = moduleOp->getContext();
385  registerContext(*mlirCtx, maxContext);
386
387  auto telemetryContext = maxContext->get<GML::MaxEngineTelemetryContext>();
388
389  // Must precede the telemetry diagnostic handler.
390  llvm::SourceMgr sourceMgr;
391  mlir::SourceMgrDiagnosticHandler diagHandler(sourceMgr, mlirCtx);
392
393  GML::MaxEngineTelemetryScope<GML::MaxEngineErrorCode::GraphLoweringError>
394      loweringDiagScope(mlirCtx, telemetryContext);
395
396  // Gather all the options from all the sources.
397  MO::GCPipelineOptions gcPipelineOptions;
398  overrideLoweringOptions(gcPipelineOptions);
399
400  // Set iff Python `Analysis::seed_kernel_decls` already seeded kernel decls,
401  // so mogg-import-packages can be skipped.
402  if ((*moduleOp)->hasAttr(MOGG::kOpaqueTypeMappingAttrName))
403    gcPipelineOptions.kernelDeclsPrePopulated = true;
404
405  // Before the cache key, so tile and non-tile compiles never collide.
406  if (impl->mofConfig && impl->mofConfig->tileBasedFusion)
407    enableTileBasedFusion(*moduleOp);
408
409  bool enableMEFMetadata = impl->getEnableMEFMetadata();
410
411  auto baseCacheDirOr = M::getMaxCacheDir();
412
413  if (!isModelIRCacheEnabled() || !baseCacheDirOr)
414    return convertMOToMEF(*moduleOp, gcPipelineOptions, enableMEFMetadata);
415
416  const std::filesystem::path &baseCacheDir = *baseCacheDirOr;
417  auto mefBackendOr = Cache::getLocalDefaultBackendChain(
418      (baseCacheDir / "mof" / "mef").string(),
419      std::string(M::getModularVersionString()));
420
421  if (mefBackendOr.isError()) {
422    return convertMOToMEF(*moduleOp, gcPipelineOptions, enableMEFMetadata);
423  }
424
425  auto keyHashOr = computeMEFCacheKey(*moduleOp, gcPipelineOptions, maxContext);
426  if (keyHashOr.isError())
427    return keyHashOr.takeError();
428  std::string keyHash = keyHashOr.takeValue();
429
430  auto mefCache = RCRef<Cache::TransformCache>::create(*mefBackendOr);
431  auto maybeMefOr = mefCache->findKeyedSync(keyHash);
432  if (maybeMefOr.isError())
433    return maybeMefOr.takeError();
434  std::optional<BufferRef> maybeMef = maybeMefOr.takeValue();
435  if (maybeMef) {
436    auto onHitLambda = Cache::CacheTelemetryContext::getTelemetryOnHitLambda(
437        "mof::M_compileToBinaryFromSource");
438    onHitLambda(*moduleOp);
439
440    return std::move(*maybeMef);
441  }
442
443  auto onMissLambda = Cache::CacheTelemetryContext::getTelemetryOnMissLambda(
444      "mof::M_compileToBinaryFromSource",
445      "mof.compiletobinaryfromsource.cache.miss.time",
446      {{"pipeline", "mof::M_compileToBinaryFromSource"}});
447  onMissLambda(*moduleOp);
448
449  auto outBufOr =
450      convertMOToMEF(*moduleOp, gcPipelineOptions, enableMEFMetadata);
451  if (outBufOr.isError())
452    return outBufOr.takeError();
453  BufferRef outputBuffer = outBufOr.takeValue();
454
455  // Insertion failure is ignored.
456  (void)mefCache->insertKeyedSync(keyHash, outputBuffer.copy());
457
458  return outputBuffer;
459}

356static ErrorOr<BufferRef> convertMOToMEF(ModuleOp moduleOp,
357                                         const MO::GCPipelineOptions &options,
358                                         bool enableMEFMetadata) {
359  bool const dumpStages = !getMaxIRDumpDir().empty();
360  GraphApiDiagnosticHandler diagnostics(moduleOp.getContext());
361  if (failed(MO::runGCPipeline(moduleOp, options, dumpStages)))
362    return Error(Twine("Graph compilation failed:\n") +
363                 diagnostics.formatMessage());
364
365  // Nothing to export without the JIT; erroring also keeps the half-lowered
366  // result out of the MEF cache. emit-mojo already wrote the Mojo.
367  if (options.preJit)
368    return Error("compilation stopped after emitting Mojo, as requested by "
369                 "pre-jit; the emitted Mojo is in ir-output-dir");
370
371  auto bufOr = MO::convertMGPToMEF(moduleOp, enableMEFMetadata);
372  if (bufOr)
373    return bufOr.takeError();
374  return bufOr.takeValue();
375}

Check your understanding: does every call to a method named compile run compiler passes?

No. The configured MEF import path can read an artifact, and the native frontend can return a cached MEF. Both paths ultimately provide compiled-model objects for initialization.

5. Transform compiler representations

The graph passes through several representations because different decisions need different information. High-level algebra and shapes are useful early; structured iteration and memory access support fusion; runtime models expose allocation, lifetime, and execution requirements.

The stage explorer describes the pass schedule proven by this checkout. It does not assert a particular fused Llama kernel or a GPU speedup. Such claims need a concrete graph/target dump and, for speed, a measured run.

Follow the compiler representations

Graph-level preparation

INPUT

mo.graph containing high-level operations, types, symbols, and device information

TRANSFORMATION

Legalize RMO; simplify; run configured shape/constant work; infer layouts and validate devices.

OUTPUT

Prepared graph before MO-to-MAP conversion

Static text diagram
Graph IR -> MO preparation -> MOToMAP -> MAP fusion/outlining
         -> MAPToMOGG -> MOGG routines -> MOGGToMGP
         -> MGP resource planning + Mojo emission
         -> kernel JIT + runtime-call lowering -> MEF serialization

Pass scheduling is source-proven. A specific fused kernel needs a concrete dump.

MO: prepare graph operations

buildMoPipeline() loads missing kernel declarations, legalizes RMO operations, and performs canonicalization and common-subexpression elimination. Options control shape inference, constant folding, and named pattern fusion. Layout inference and device validation prepare the graph for subsequent lowering.

This is distinct from Graph.output() verification: a structurally valid graph still needs target-aware compilation and lowering.

219void M::MO::buildMoPipeline(mlir::OpPassManager &pm,
220                            const MoPipelineOptions &opts) {
221  auto kernelLibraryPaths =
222      llvm::to_vector_of<std::string>(opts.kernelLibraryPaths);
223
224  // Skipped when the caller already seeded decls and
225  // `mogg.opaque_type_mapping` via `MOGG::copyKernelDecls`. RewriteOpaqueTypes
226  // still runs so freshly-cloned `!mo.opaque<"simple">` uses get rewritten.
227  if (!opts.kernelDeclsPrePopulated) {
228    pm.addPass(MOGG::createImportPackages(
229        {.mojoPkgPaths = kernelLibraryPaths, .litMlirPaths = {}}));
230    pm.addPass(MOGG::createVerifyKernels());
231  }
232
233  pm.addPass(MOGG::createRewriteOpaqueTypes());
234  pm.addPass(KGEN::createVerifyParameters());
235
236  if (opts.debugPrintAllTensors)
237    pm.addPass(MO::createDebugPrintAllTensorsPass());
238
239  pm.addPass(RMO::createLegalizeRMOOps());
240
241  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());
242  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
243  pm.addPass(MO::createCanonicalizeChainSequences());
244
245  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
246  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());
247
248  std::string_view compiledFrameworkLabel;
249  if (opts.compiledFrameworkLabel.hasValue())
250    compiledFrameworkLabel = opts.compiledFrameworkLabel;
251
252  std::optional<std::string> cacheDir;
253  if (opts.cacheDir.hasValue())
254    cacheDir = opts.cacheDir;
255
256  if (opts.useShapeInference)
257    buildShapeInferencePipeline(pm);
258
259  // TODO(GEX-886): Remove symbolic optimization's dependency on constant
260  // folding.
261  if (opts.constantFold)
262    pm.addPass(MO::createConstantFoldPass(compiledFrameworkLabel, cacheDir,
263                                          kernelLibraryPaths));
264
265  pm.addPass(MO::createHoistConstantSubgraphsIntoParent());
266  pm.addNestedPass<MO::GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());
267

MAP: expose and combine structured computation

After MOToMAP, structured kernels make iteration and access relationships available to the compiler. MAP fusion combines eligible work; later passes handle accumulating buffers and views before outlining kernel bodies.

A Llama residual addition is visible in TransformerBlock.__call__(). Whether it becomes a separate runtime kernel, merges into an epilogue, or participates in another transformation depends on the concrete graph, dtype, target, and eligible patterns. Reading createFuseKernels() in the schedule proves that the fusion pass is invoked, not which final kernels it produces.

buildMapPipelineFuse eligible structured computations and outline kernel bodies.SOURCE31 lines

338void M::MO::buildMapPipeline(mlir::OpPassManager &pm,
339                             const MapPipelineOptions &opts) {
340  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
341  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());
342
343  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(MAP::createFuseKernels());
344  if (opts.fuseMutableLoadStore)
345    pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(MAP::createFuseMutableLoads());
346  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
347  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());
348
349  // After fusion settles, give every fused-output epilogue a real store pointer
350  // (plus a pre-cast accumulation buffer for mixed-precision accumulation).
351  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(MAP::createAllocateAccumulatingBuffers());
352
353  // An unfused reshape has no MAPToMOGG lowering (its hoisted stride op isn't
354  // LowerableToMOGGInterface yet), and an unfused contiguous slice can take the
355  // zero-copy path. Raise both back before outlining commits to MAP.
356  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(MAP::createRaiseBackContiguousViews());
357
358  pm.addPass(MAP::createOutlineStructuredKernelBodies());
359  // Uniques `map.iter.opaque` inputs and captures so the lowered kernel's
360  // parameter list is minimal.
361  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
362  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(MAP::createLoopInvariantViewMotion());
363  // CSE before canonicalize: two loads hoisting the same view create identical
364  // stride ops; CSE must unify them so DedupeCapturingClosureCaptures can fold
365  // the duplicate captures.
366  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());
367  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
368}

MOGG: prepare kernel routines

MAPToMOGG lowers structured bodies into the next representation. buildMoggPipeline() legalizes rowwise kernels, conforms call operands, outlines routines, and wraps functions for tracing. The module is then ready for MOGGToMGP.

370void M::MO::buildMoggPipeline(mlir::OpPassManager &pm,
371                              const MoggPipelineOptions &) {

376
377  // On the module, not GraphOp: the outlined stubs are its siblings.

MGP: plan runtime work and emit Mojo

This stage reasons about model execution resources: buffer reuse, allocation planning and deferral, model arguments, dependency chains, and runtime primitives. It also handles marked device graphs and merges equivalent routines before emitting Mojo.

Graph-level activation/temporary-buffer planning is a different responsibility from the serving KV-cache manager's request/page policy. Both concern memory, but their objects and lifetimes differ.

JIT and MEF: finish the artifact

gcPipelineImpl() connects the builders with explicit conversions. After MGP processing and Mojo emission, it schedules JitCompileKernels, strips kernel declarations, and finishes JIT lowering. runGCPipeline() constructs the pass manager and calls pm.run(); adding passes alone does not execute them.

MEF serialization occurs in the frontend after successful pipeline execution. A MEF-backed CompiledModel is a compiled artifact. It is not yet the weight-initialized engine Model used for token execution.

638LogicalResult M::MO::runGCPipeline(ModuleOp moduleOp,
639                                   const GCPipelineOptions &opts,
640                                   bool dumpIntermediates) {
641  auto pm = mlir::PassManager::on<ModuleOp>(
642      moduleOp.getContext(), mlir::OpPassManager::Nesting::Implicit);
643
644  if (!opts.mlirTimingOutDir.empty()) {
645    auto enabledTiming = M::configureMLIRPassTimingJSONOutput(
646        pm, opts.mlirTimingOutDir.getValue(), "GC Pipeline");
647    if (enabledTiming.isError()) {
648      llvm::errs() << enabledTiming.getError() << "\n";
649      return failure();
650    }
651  }
652
653  gcPipelineImpl(pm, opts, /*skipJit=*/opts.preJit, dumpIntermediates);
654  return pm.run(moduleOp);
655}

Observation point What to inspect Evidence needed
Before native compile Graph signature, output types, devices, named weight declarations Source or a graph-building run
Stage boundaries mo-pre-map, mo-to-map, map-pre-mogg, map-to-mogg, mogg-pre-mgp, mogg-to-mgp, mgp Actual IR dumps for the chosen graph/target
After Mojo emission Generated routines; pre_jit can intentionally stop before JIT Source-matched compile inspection
After MEF creation Artifact and model interfaces Compile result
Runtime performance Kernel launches, allocation/copy behavior, latency GPU run with workload and target metadata

pre_jit deliberately ends before a runnable artifact can be serialized. The frontend reports that requested stop; it is different from claiming the entire graph compiled successfully.

Check your understanding: does one transformer layer imply one GPU kernel?

No. A layer contains many operations. Compiler fusion, outlining, and routine reuse determine a different structure, while kernels can launch their own target-specific work. The final kernel set must be inspected for the concrete graph and target.

6. Initialize, execute, and reuse

Initialization combines the compiled artifact with weight buffers and runtime state. Execution supplies the current batch's inputs to that instance. The Python session checks expected weight names and CPU/device category when that metadata is available, checks buffer contiguity, and enters the native load path. The engine's continuation constructs executable models on a CPU runtime worker.

The full init_all() also contains a virtual-device branch that returns compile-only stand-ins. This chapter's executable model path assumes the required real target device is available.

310AsyncValueRef<ExecutableModels>
311Engine::Context::initModel(AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels> compiledModels,
312                           const WeightsRegistryRef &weightsRegistry) const {
313  auto result = AsyncValueRef<ExecutableModels>::allocate(cpuDevice);
314
315  // Use andThenAsync to ensure createExecutableModels runs on a cpuDevice
316  // worker thread.  The caller may be a foreign thread (e.g. a Python
317  // ThreadPoolExecutor thread) that has no AsyncRT cpuDevice set in its
318  // thread-local storage; MGP_RT_BufferBorrowV2 (called during Model::setup)
319  // requires a valid current cpuDevice.
320  std::move(compiledModels)
321      .andThenAsync(
322          [result = result.copy(), weights = weightsRegistry.copy(),
323           this](AsyncValueRef<CompiledModels> &&compiledModelsRef) mutable {
324            if (compiledModelsRef.isError())
325              return setUnknownLocError(
326                  std::move(result),
327                  compiledModelsRef.takeDiagnostic().getMessage().copy());
328
329            auto executableModelsOr =
330                createExecutableModels(compiledModelsRef.get(), cpuDevice,
331                                       getConfig(), weights.getPointer());
332            if (executableModelsOr.isError())
333              return setUnknownLocError(std::move(result),
334                                        executableModelsOr.takeError());
335
336            std::move(result).emplace(executableModelsOr.takeValue());
337          });
338
339  return result;
340}

Per-batch execution is a small call boundary

LlamaModelBase.execute() receives already prepared buffers, calls the initialized model, and delegates interpretation of its output buffers to the batch processor. The graph-building and compiler methods are not called in this method.

Prefill and decode change the inputs

Use the two-sequence illustration below to see what changes at the graph boundary. Token IDs are invented examples; they are not captured model output. The logical KV history grows between steps, while the runtime supplies the appropriate KV buffers/metadata through the declared input subtree.

Sequence A contributes three tokens; B contributes two. The model uses row offsets to locate each sequence inside the packed token buffer.

KV leaves: buffers/metadata declared by kv_params; carry the cache state.

Changing concrete token values or lengths within the supported symbolic contract does not itself alter the Python layer definitions. Changes to architecture, dtype, devices, output policy, or specialization settings need the corresponding compatible graph/artifact. This is not a universal promise that every possible shape change avoids compilation.

Cached compilation still has a trace in this route

compile_and_init_graphs() calls GraphSpec.trace() before compile_reusing_mefs(). Therefore a configured MEF import or native cache hit can skip graph compiler work after tracing has already happened. Other MAX artifact-loading APIs may enter at a different point.

In this GraphSpec route, all three paths have already traced the graph.

Device-graph finalization is another mechanism

The ordinary GraphSpec defaults is_device_graph=False. FinalizeDeviceGraphsPass runs within MGP processing but returns immediately for an unmarked model. For a marked model, it finalizes device-graph collectives after the staging/build-stub pipeline. That work is separate from the output signature and mo.output installed by Python.

CUDA graph capture/replay also concerns replaying device work. It should not be used as another name for constructing or finalizing a MAX Graph.

Diagnose the boundary first

Symptom First code to inspect Question
Graph output/verification error Graph.output() Are the output values, chains, and signature valid?
Native compilation failure _compile_module() → frontend → compiler diagnostics Which representation, target rule, or lowering failed?
Weight initialization failure InferenceSession.init_all() Are names, device categories, and buffer layouts compatible?
Incorrect inference values Model execution and a reference implementation Does numerical behavior match for the same inputs/configuration?
Unexpected startup time Trace, compilation, artifact reuse, and initialization separately Which phase actually ran, and was an artifact reused?

Check your understanding: what is the complete lifecycle in one sentence?

MAX resolves the Llama configuration, records its symbolic computation, finalizes the graph's interface, compiles or resolves an artifact, initializes executable state with weights, and executes that model on prepared batch buffers.
